source.doc: FHWA-NHI-17-071, Strut-and-Tie Modeling (STM) for Concrete Structures, Design Examples (NHI Course No. 130126), FHWA National Highway Institute, October 2017
source.design_basis: AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 8th Edition - NOT ACI 318-19. Statics, topology, member forces, and angles are code-agnostic; node-face capacities (phi*Pn) below use AASHTO phi = 0.70 (compression) / 0.90 (tension) and AASHTO Table 5.8.2.5.3a-1 efficiency factors, so they validate the node-geometry construction and stress arithmetic, not ACI 318-19 Table 23.9.2 numbers.
source.extraction_note: Every number below was read directly from the fetched PDF (Figures 1-1, 1-8, 1-12, 1-15, 1-21; Table 1-1; Design Steps 4-10). Nothing is derived or fabricated.

geometry_in.note: a = As*fy/(0.85*f'c*b) = 20.32*60/(0.85*5*48) = 5.98 in, rounded to 6 in. hSTM = 72 - 5 - 3 = 64 in (5 = 4.90 rounded). All bearing plates increased from 12 in to 14 in during the Node F strut-interface check.

loads_kips.load_positions: each load at 1.5h = 108 in from its adjacent bearing centerline; loads 108 in apart
loads_kips.self_weight: included in the stated point loads

reinforcement.bottom_tie: 16 No. 10 bars (As = 20.32 in^2), two rows of 8, 2 in bottom cover, No. 5 stirrups, tie centroid 4.90 in above bottom fiber; ends hooked
reinforcement.vertical_tie_BD_region: 9 sets of 2 No. 5 closed stirrups (4 legs/set) at 6 in over available length la = 48 in; Ast provided = 11.16 in^2
reinforcement.crack_control_vertical: 2 No. 5 closed stirrups (4 legs) at 8 in (Av = 1.86 in^2/ft >= 1.73 in^2/ft)
reinforcement.top_strut_steel: 6 No. 8 (Ast = 4.74 in^2) added because back face of Node F was deficient (required 4.67 in^2)

truss_topology.nodes: A = left support (tie level), B = tie level under vertical tie at 54 in, C = right support; D above B, E under left load, F under right load (all at hSTM = 64 in above tie)
truss_topology.left_half: two-panel model (vertical tie BD) - used for demonstration only
truss_topology.right_half: direct strut model (single inclined strut CF)

angles_deg.note: 30.7 = atan(600/1013); strut lengths from Figure 1-8: AD/BE = 83.7 in (typ), CF = 125.5 in

node_C_CCT.back_face: not checked - bond stresses from deformed-bar development need not be applied to the back face of a CCT node (AASHTO 5.8.2.5.3b)

node_checks.node_A_CCT: adequate by inspection: same bearing as C, strut AD = 785 kips < 1177 kips and wider interface (49.8 deg)

back_face.fix: top strut reinforced with 6 No. 8; deficiency 157 kips, Ast required = 157/(0.80*0.70*60) = 4.67 in^2, provided 4.74 in^2

node_checks.node_E: resultant of DE and BE components: R = sqrt(1013^2 + 600^2) = 1177 kips at 30.7 deg - statically equivalent to Node F, therefore OK
node_checks.nodes_B_D: smeared nodes - not checked (tie force spread over available length la)

anchorage.available_calc: x + lb + overhang - cover = 8.4 + 14 + 5 - 2 (x = 5/tan(30.7) = 8.4 in from bearing edge to critical section where tie centroid exits the extended nodal zone)

tolerances.member_forces: 2% (published values rounded to whole kips; forces scale with 1/z, so the published z = 64 in must be used - see topology_note)
tolerances.node_capacities_phiPn: 2% (requires AASHTO phi = 0.70 and AASHTO efficiency factors, m = 1.0)

topology_note: This example maps onto the calculator's funicular arch-and-tie model directly. The document itself states (page 1-28, 'Static Equivalency') that the left-half two-panel model is interchangeable with a direct strut, so the canonical symmetric model of this beam is the three-segment funicular polygon for two equal point loads: springing strut A->E at 30.7 deg, horizontal crown segment E->F carrying the constant thrust, and springing strut F->C at 30.7 deg, with a constant bottom tie A->C. The published forces satisfy the funicular identity exactly: H = M_max/z = 64,800 kip-in / 64 in = 1,012.5 ~ 1,013 kips = tie force BC = crown chord EF; springing force = H/cos(30.7) = 1,177 kips = CF; springing angle = atan(hSTM/a) = atan(64/108) = 30.7 deg = atan(R/H) = atan(600/1013). For a single point load the funicular polygon degenerates to the classic two-strut triangle; for the two loads here it is the trapezoid above. To reproduce these numbers the engine must be run with the published chord geometry (tie centroid 5 in above bottom, crown depth a = 6 in, z = 64 in) rather than its own f_ce-sized crown, because the FHWA example sizes the top strut by the Whitney block (a = As*fy/(0.85*f'c*b)); with z pinned at 64 in all member forces above are closed-form statics and code-independent. Node-stress expected values validate the node construction geometry (w = lb*sin(theta) + ha*cos(theta), ha = 2 x cover-to-tie-centroid at CCT supports, ha = strut depth a at the CCC load node) but carry AASHTO phi/nu factors, not ACI 318-19 beta_n; compare geometry and Acn directly, capacities only under AASHTO factors.
